title: Revolutionary Roman Republic
capsule: The Roman Republic, established traditionally in 509 BC after the expulsion of the Tarquin kings, was governed by two annually elected consuls, the Senate, and a complex of popular assemblies that mediated the long struggle between patricians and plebeians, concluded by the mid-third century BC. At its apex the Republic controlled the entire Mediterranean basin: the three Punic Wars (264–146 BC) eliminated Carthage, and campaigns in Macedonia, Greece, Asia Minor, and Gaul added vast provinces. The Republic's institutions collapsed under the strain of slave-worked latifundia, the Social War (91–87 BC), and the successive dictatorships of Sulla, Caesar, and the triumviral period; Octavian's defeat of Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BC effectively ended republican government, and he assumed the title Augustus in 27 BC.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Republican-era Roman boundaries are reconstructed from literary sources (Livy, Polybius), inscriptions, and archaeological surveys; provincial boundaries after the mid-second century BC are relatively well attested, but earlier extent in Italy and during the conquest period involves scholarly inference.
